Its range lies in the middle-high register, each gong pot sounding a different pitch, so the layers are rich. When several mallets strike at once the sound is dense and flowing, with a wave-like resonance. A single pot is warm with a metallic sheen; several together make a complex, interwoven sound. Beside the steadiness and weight of Javanese gamelan the reyong is lighter and more nimble; beside the glockenspiel of Western percussion it keeps more of the organic texture and resonance of tradition, with a more human warmth, and it blends easily into the overall fabric of the gamelan.
